import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.cluster import SpectralClustering
from sklearn.metrics.pairwise import cosine_similarity

MAX_DRIVERS = 5

def design(feats):
    # Identify highly associated features (p < 0.05, |t| > 2.5)
    sig_mask = np.abs(feats.x.T @ feats.y) / np.sqrt(np.sum(feats.y * (1 - feats.y))) > 2.5
    sig_ids = [feats.ids[i] for i in range(len(feats.ids)) if sig_mask[i]]
    
    # If no significant features, return empty design
    if not sig_ids:
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Build correlation matrix for significant features
    X_sig = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in sig_ids]]
    corr_matrix = np.corrcoef(X_sig.T)
    
    # Cluster features with high correlations (>0.6)
    mask = np.abs(corr_matrix) >= 0.6
    np.fill_diagonal(mask, False)
    
    # Use spectral clustering to group correlated features
    try:
        clustering = SpectralClustering(n_clusters=1, affinity='precomputed', 
                                       random_state=0).fit(mask.astype(float))
        cluster_labels = clustering.labels_
        if len(set(cluster_labels)) == 1:
            # No meaningful clusters found, use top features
            cluster_labels = np.zeros(len(sig_ids))
    except:
        # Fallback to simple approach
        cluster_labels = np.zeros(len(sig_ids))
    
    # Select representative features from each cluster
    selected_features = []
    for cl in set(cluster_labels):
        cl_indices = np.where(cluster_labels == cl)[0]
        cl_features = [sig_ids[i] for i in cl_indices]
        
        # Choose the feature with highest absolute t-statistic
        t_stats = [abs(stats.ttest_ind(feats.x[feats.y==1, feats.column(fid)], 
                                     feats.x[feats.y==0, feats.column(fid)])[0]) 
                  for fid in cl_features]
        best_idx = cl_indices[np.argmax(t_stats)]
        selected_features.append(sig_ids[best_idx])
    
    # Remove near-duplicates (correlated with r > 0.9)
    unique_features = []
    for fid in selected_features:
        is_unique = True
        for uf in unique_features:
            col1 = feats.column(fid)
            col2 = feats.column(uf)
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0,1]) > 0.9:
                is_unique = False
                break
        if is_unique:
            unique_features.append(fid)
    
    # Select top features by effect size
    if len(unique_features) > 0:
        # Compute effect sizes (mean difference)
        effect_sizes = []
        for fid in unique_features:
            col = feats.column(fid)
            mean_y1 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, col])
            mean_y0 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, col])
            effect_sizes.append(abs(mean_y1 - mean_y0))
        
        # Sort by effect size
        sorted_indices = np.argsort(effect_sizes)[::-1][:MAX_DRIVERS]
        drivers = tuple([unique_features[i] for i in sorted_indices])
    else:
        drivers = ()
    
    # For scoring, use all selected features as columns
    columns = tuple(unique_features)
    
    # Create product terms for pairs of selected features
    products = []
    for i in range(len(columns)):
        for j in range(i+1, len(columns)):
            products.append((columns[i], columns[j]))
    
    # Weighted score using top features
    loadings = {}
    for fid in columns:
        col = feats.column(fid)
        # Weight by standardized effect size
        mean_y1 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==1, col])
        mean_y0 = np.mean(feats.x[feats.y==0, col])
        loadings[fid] = mean_y1 - mean_y0
    
    return Design(drivers=drivers, columns=columns, products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
